name: cmux
works_with: Any terminal agent: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Aider and more
short: A Mac terminal with vertical tabs that lights up the pane where a coding agent needs you.
what: A native macOS terminal built on libghostty, the engine behind Ghostty. When an agent needs your attention, its pane gets a blue ring and its tab lights up in a sidebar that also shows the git branch, PR status, folder and ports. It has a built-in browser your agent can drive, SSH workspaces and a CLI for scripting.
who: Mac users who run several coding agent sessions at once and lose track of which one is waiting. It's macOS only for now.
needs: A Mac. cmux is a native Swift and AppKit app
Optional: Homebrew, for the second install method
Your agent CLIs installed first, if you want cmux to set up session resume for them

steps.title: Install from the DMG
steps.text: Download `cmux-macos.dmg` from the latest GitHub release, open it and drag cmux into Applications. It updates itself after that.

steps.title: Or install with Homebrew
steps.code:
brew tap manaflow-ai/cmux
brew install --cask cmux

steps.title: First launch
steps.text: macOS may ask you to confirm opening an app from an identified developer. Click Open. It reads your existing Ghostty config for themes and fonts.

steps.title: Let agent sessions resume after a restart
steps.text: This sets up hooks for the agents it can find and prints what it skipped.

try.label: From the README
try.text:
Run two agents side by side (⌘ D splits right). When one stops to wait for you, its pane gets a blue ring. Press ⌘ ⇧ U to jump to the latest unread one.

For a remote machine: cmux ssh user@remote

watch: Browser import can copy cookies, history and sessions from Chrome, Firefox, Arc and other browsers into cmux. It's optional, so only use it if you want those logins inside cmux.
When you reopen cmux it can run your agents' resume commands automatically. Turn off Settings > Terminal > Resume Agent Sessions on Reopen if you'd rather it didn't.
`cmux hooks setup` changes the hook settings of the agents it finds.
The README says tokens, passwords, secrets and API keys are dropped from saved resume settings.
